notes: Training Zone: a knife step in the stealth room — creep up behind a dummy and stab it with Ghost's Monoblade

Training Zone: no hotbar, one weapon at a time — each part issues its own (sidearm, then a new gun every live-fire round, a stun pistol for stealth, a cyberweapon for netrunning, a minigun for the boss)
Training Zone armory now fits attachments to your weapon; new cyberweapon step
Training Zone: a graduation-exam boss — THE INSTRUCTOR guards the exit with a pylon-powered shield and three phases (easier each time you fall)

Training Zone: live-fire drills — bots that shoot back, five rounds that get harder (stationary gunners, movers, a heavy, a riot shield with a sniper and a drone, then everything with grenades and a rusher)
You cannot die in the drills: a fall restarts the round a little easier, and three falls wave you through
New: Training Zone on the title menu — a practice facility that walks you through every mechanic, never touches your save
Every weapon in the Training Zone is yellow and black practice gear wearing the Training Zone logo
Body armor: buy a vest for an armor bar that soaks up damage
Gun attachments: suppressor, extended magazine, laser sight, stabilizer, hollow points
Experience and nine perks in three trees
Dash through a shot for a perfect dodge
Medals and XP after every operation
Press Y to scan: devices, caches and lamps show through walls
Lamps and shadow: guards see you from less far in the dark, shoot lamps out
Hackable devices: decoy speakers, overload panels, vending machines
Choose a daemon bonus after every terminal hack
Grab an alerted guard as a hostage: the others hold fire
Awareness rings over suspicious guards
Take a guard's uniform to walk past patrols, and interrogate tied guards for intel
Guards can run to alarm panels to call reinforcements: stop them or disable the panel
Vents let you crawl between two points unseen
Security cameras and breaker boxes in operations: shoot a camera or cut the power
Locked caches and stashes: a lockpick minigame
Cyberware at the Black Market, including the Reflex Booster slow-motion on B
A Crafting tab turns Weapon Parts into lockpicks and consumables
Silent work: hold E behind a guard to choke them. Let go for a knockout, hold too long and they die
Zip-tie, search, carry and hide bodies. Guards who find a body raise the alarm
Press T to whistle, and throw Noisemakers to lure patrols
Nonlethal weapons now knock out instead of killing
Cyberdeck: every hack now spends RAM from your deck
Two new hacking games: a HEX SEQUENCE grid and a COMMAND PROMPT
Upgrade your deck and buy nine mods at a Black Market stall
Press Z to PING and mark hostiles nearby

Black Markets are now hidden: ten stalls in the middle of the alleys, out of sight of the streets and not marked in the world, with the nearest a long walk from your start. The minimap points the way with pink diamonds and edge arrows

The Black Market is no longer in the pause menu: fifteen Black Market stalls now stand in the alleys of the open city (a pink dot on the minimap, E at the counter). There is no market during an operation, so buy before you go

Interiors are much more detailed and unique: three layouts per type, counters with someone behind them, 12 new kinds of furniture, a different floor in every room, the name of the place on the wall, windows onto the night city, and ceiling fittings that move. Door frames are coloured by what is behind them

Every building in the open city now has a door: press E to go inside. Apartments, noodle bars, clinics, offices, warehouses, server rooms, clubs and every named landmark, each generated from its district and size
People inside have something to say, stashes can be searched once for credits, and the glowing door takes you back to the street where you stood
The Helix trace is much harder: it climbs faster, barely recovers (not at all right after a hunt), locks harder, and intrusions start earlier with a shorter window
The Helix trace is harder: it climbs faster, falls slower, locks harder and its intrusions come earlier and give you less time
Nuallink: Ghost's implant is now a link with an inbox of calls and messages from the cast (press N, or open it from the pause menu or the Journal)
Helix now traces your link while enemies hunt you: at full trace it locks the line and sends a squad; press V to raise a firewall against its intrusions
ASCENSION speaks on the link after Chapter 4 and can mark or freeze nearby hostiles on V; Clawd briefs every operation, translated by CrustAI
Ghost Mode switches the link off; the Dossier has a new section on the numbers

Missions get complications from act 2 on (act 1 on Hard): blackouts, reinforcements on the first alarm, a tripped alarm that keeps sending squads, turrets, and snipers whose red laser gives you a moment to sidestep
Four new enemy types: snipers, shield troops (shots bounce off their shield from the front), rushers that lunge, and fixed turrets that an EMP stuns
Complications show in the briefing and as chips at the top of the screen; fast enemy shots can no longer skip past you between frames

Missions now have twists: plant charges and outrun the fuse, assassinate an armoured officer, hunt a keycard, free a hostage who follows you out, hold a lockdown ring against waves, hold an upload or outrun a reactor overload, and survive ambushes at pickups
The briefing, objective panel, markers, prompts and timers show each twist; reinforcements arrive from out of sight when you trip one

New character creator laid out like a civic-records terminal: three lifepaths on animated cards, appearance rows with presets, attribute points and a difficulty window, with boot, scan and sealing animations
Backgrounds are now three lifepaths (Lantern Row Kid, Helix Contractor, Glass Wastes Courier) plus five attributes; older characters are converted automatically and no progress is lost

New Dossier: a searchable 10,800-word handbook (title menu, Journal, or H in the creator) that explains every number; extract passages as notes, save the whole text, or export your own character record (opens the share sheet in the Android app)
New first-person weapons modelled by hand in Blender: pistol, SMG, rifle, shotgun, sniper rifle and a combat knife, each with real detail and a lit edge or coil strip, carried in gloved fists
The knife is held tilted so the blade's flat faces you
Overhauled HUD: implant-level badge, thick health bar with current and max, dash pips, framed minimap with a COMBAT / SUSPICIOUS threat bar, and a quest tracker with one short yellow objective
Landmark discoveries now open as a card inside the HUD (and are translated), instead of a floating pop-up
Ammo now reads magazine | reserve with the weapon's silhouette; Reload and Use-item prompts appear when they matter
New difficulty: Hardcore — half the ammo, no map markers, and a failed operation ends the run for good (endings stay unlocked)
Much lighter city: far buildings, pedestrians, guards and cars are culled, so free roam runs faster
Ammunition now has a carry limit per type

Missions, arenas and story scenes that happen indoors now play in hand-drawn levels instead of random rooms: office, clinic, warehouse, factory, metro, underdeep caves, club, records vault, server halls, a network lattice and orbital stations
Boss, arena and defend fights have hand-placed cover, indoors and out in the streets
Story scenes in Noah's clinic, clubs, offices, metro platforms, bars and small flats play in their own interiors
Ghost's apartment is rebuilt as a lived-in bedroom: posters, blinds, a bedside lamp, a rug, plants and a neon sign
New Avalon is now a hand-drawn city: real district shapes, authored blocks and landmark sites instead of random generation
New building types: shop rows with alleys, twin slabs, podium towers, courtyards, container yards and warehouses
Three facade looks (office grid, ribbon shopfronts, dim industrial sheds); Lantern Row and the Gray Market are strung with lanterns and signs
